summary: Persistent caching for ReactiveUI apps with explicit serializer and SQLite-provider configuration.
recommendedPatterns: Initialize Akavache with the builder pattern.
Keep Akavache behind repository or service abstractions.
avoidPatterns: Do not hide caching policy directly in views.
Do not scatter unstable cache keys throughout the codebase.
setupSteps: Add Akavache.Sqlite3 and a serializer package.
Configure the cache database through the builder.
Use the appropriate cache buckets intentionally.
commonPitfalls: Treating the cache like an unversioned key-value junk drawer.

features: Memory, local-machine, user-account, and secure caches
Settings, image/drawing, and HTTP download helpers
options: In-memory, SQLite, or encrypted SQLite backend
packageSelection: Start with Akavache plus one storage provider and one generic serializer.
Prefer Akavache.Sqlite3 + Akavache.SystemTextJson for a general lean application.
Use Akavache.EncryptedSqlite3 only when encrypted-at-rest cache semantics are required.
Add Settings, Drawing, or HttpDownloader only for those specialized helpers.
sourceGeneratorGuidance: Use ReactiveUI.SourceGenerators for state/commands around cache operations and generated Refit clients for remote fetches.
Akavache cache serialization/provider behavior remains runtime configuration.
compatibilityNotes: Initialize a generic serializer and call WithSqliteProvider before default registrations when SQLite is selected.
Cache observables can be consumed through lean ReactiveUI.Primitives; retain System.Reactive only when a public compatibility contract requires it.
migrationGuidance: Centralize legacy BlobCache startup in Registrations.Start and explicit provider/serializer configuration.
Migrate Rx composition around cache operations to Primitives operators while preserving keys, expiration, invalidation, and fetch ordering with tests.
